place_fields.vibe: Scenic sunrise hill with historic fort heritage
place_fields.summary: Nandi Hills is a historic hill destination near Bengaluru known for sunrise views, scenic landscapes, Tipu's Drop and fort remains.

planning_attributes.description: Nandi Hills, formerly Nandidurga, is about 1,478 metres above sea level and has historic fortifications, viewpoints and Tipu's Drop.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Nandi Hills was used as Tipu Sultan's summer retreat; the hill also retains fort walls, gates and viewpoints.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: From Bengaluru, travel by road toward Chikkaballapur; the district tourism site says the hill is about 60 km from Bengaluru and can be reached via Chikkaballapur by vehicle.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Official tourism information lists visitor entry timings of 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM; busy periods may have traffic or visitor-management restrictions.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The hill can be crowded on weekends; early arrival is recommended. Use care around steep viewpoints such as Tipu's Drop.
planning_attributes.notes: The supplied point is identified by the request as Nandi hills trekking spot; the supplied coordinates are preserved exactly.

place_fields.vibe: Pre-dawn sunrise trek with mountain and cloud views
place_fields.summary: Skandagiri, also called Kalavara Durga, is a rocky hill trek near Bengaluru known for sunrise views, a sea-of-clouds effect and historic fort ruins.
place_fields.best_time: Winter, especially September to February; avoid monsoon conditions when rocks become slippery

planning_attributes.description: Skandagiri rises to about 1,350 metres and has an approximately 8 km trail with steep inclines and rocky boulders.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The hill is historically associated with Kalwarbetta/Kalavara Durga and an abandoned fort attributed to Tipu Sultan's period; the fort was abandoned after 1791.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Karnataka Tourism says Skandagiri is about 70 km from Bengaluru; travel toward Chikkaballapur and reach the trek starting point at Kalawara village.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: A trek booking/permission through Karnataka Eco-tourism is required according to Karnataka Tourism.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: The trail has steep inclines and rocky boulders. Karnataka Tourism recommends proper trekking shoes, sufficient water and a headlamp/torch for night trekking; monsoon conditions can make rocks slippery.
planning_attributes.notes: Karnataka Tourism describes most trekkers as taking 6 to 8 hours to complete the circuit.
